args.summary: The v2.3.1 deploy of checkout-api began failing health checks in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an 18% error rate. As mitigation, the service was rolled back across all production regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. Post-rollback verification: all regions running v2.3.0, service healthy, error rate reduced to 0.2%. v2.3.1 needs investigation before any redeploy.
args.title: checkout-api rollback from v2.3.1 to v2.3.0 due to failed health checks

trace.final:
All done. Here's a summary of what I did:

**1. Diagnosis**
- Latest deploy **v2.3.1** was unhealthy in all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west) with an **18% error rate**.
- Reviewing deployment history, the most recent version that was actually *healthy in production* was **v2.3.0** — I chose this over v2.3.1-rc, which was only ever healthy in *staging*, not production.

**2. Rollback**
- Rolled checkout-api back to **v2.3.0** in all production regions.
- Verified post-rollback: all three regions now on v2.3.0, service **healthy**, error rate down from 18% → **0.2%**.

**3. Incident**
- Opened **SEV2 incident INC-0001** for checkout-api describing the failed health checks, the rollback action, and the verification results. The on-call engineer has been paged.

Note: v2.3.1 remains marked unhealthy in the release history — it should not be redeployed until the root cause is investigated.
